words.sense: A neutral or involuntary interruption in an activity or process.
words.connotation: neutral or negative, implies a disruption in flow.
misconceptions: Thinking it always means a permanent end.
Confusing it with a planned vacation.

words.sense: A planned, structured, and often extended leave from work for rest or professional growth.
misconceptions: Using it for any casual or short-term time off.

semantic_axes.description: Whether the break is planned and desired (sabbatical) or circumstantial and potentially unwelcome (hiatus).
Whether the break is a formal leave of absence from a career (sabbatical) or just a gap in a sequence (hiatus).
Sabbaticals tend to be extended; a hiatus can range from brief to extended.

hiatus: The show went on a long hiatus after the lead actor fell ill.
Production was forced into a hiatus due to the unexpected power failure.
She came back to the project after a two-year hiatus.
The band took a brief hiatus, but fans hope for a reunion soon.
There was a noticeable hiatus in their communication during the conflict.
He found the hiatus in his routine to be deeply frustrating.
sabbatical: The professor used her sabbatical to complete her research in London.
He is on sabbatical this year, studying new trends in graphic design.
She planned her sabbatical months in advance to ensure her team was ready.
After ten years, the company allows employees to take a paid sabbatical.
During his sabbatical, he finally learned to speak Italian fluently.
The primary goal of her sabbatical was personal and professional rejuvenation.

edges.boundary_rule: A 'hiatus' is an unplanned or neutral interruption of activity; a 'sabbatical' is an intentional, planned, and extended professional leave.

misconceptions.M1: Assuming any break from work is a sabbatical.
misconceptions.M2: Assuming any pause in a sequence is an intentional, structured leave.
misconceptions.M3: Ignoring the element of intent and planning in defining a sabbatical.

chains.frame: What the manager put the project on: a ___

beats.text: When venture capital suddenly collapsed mid-quarter, the manager halted development on the app without any timeline for resuming.
beats.decisive_clue: venture capital suddenly collapsed mid-quarter, the manager halted development on the app without any timeline
beats.reason: An unexpected halt to an operational workflow due to an external financial shock is a hiatus; a project cannot take a sabbatical.

beats.text: With bank accounts frozen and no clear reopening date, the remaining contract staff were dismissed indefinitely.
beats.decisive_clue: accounts frozen and no clear reopening date, the remaining contract staff were dismissed indefinitely
beats.reason: Indefinite suspension and team dispersal confirm an involuntary operational disruption rather than a planned leave.

chains.feedback_short: Projects experience a hiatus when operations are interrupted; only people take sabbaticals.
chains.feedback_deep: The shutdown was forced by sudden funding loss and applies to an organizational project, making 'hiatus' the only correct term.
chains.contrast_rule: Sabbaticals are planned leaves for individuals; operational gaps and project suspensions are hiatuses.

hints.attention: Can a software project take a professional leave?
hints.axis: Whether the break is planned and desired (sabbatical) or circumstantial and potentially unwelcome (hiatus).
hints.contrast: Sabbaticals are planned leaves for individuals; operational gaps and project suspensions are hiatuses.
